title: Waldorf-inspired Early Childhood Curriculum
ageScope: Birth through age six; final pathway includes 5- and 6-year-olds through 83 months.
approach: Warm relationships, responsive rhythm, imitation, purposeful work, imaginative play, oral storytelling, arts/handwork and nature.

areas.title: Relationships & daily rhythm
areas.purpose: Predictable, responsive care and a secure connection with familiar adults.

areas.title: Movement & sensory exploration
areas.purpose: Voluntary movement, comfortable sensory experience and access to the environment.

areas.title: Practical life & purposeful work
areas.purpose: Imitation and participation in useful everyday care at an accessible level.

areas.title: Oral language, stories & verses
areas.purpose: Rich spoken/signed language, family words, gentle repetition and meaningful communication.

areas.title: Imagination, play & social connection
areas.purpose: Responsive early play, later symbolic play, construction and supported relationships.

areas.title: Arts, music & handwork
areas.purpose: Original expression through color, sound, gesture, material and making.

areas.title: Nature, seasons & community
areas.purpose: Respectful outdoor noticing, local change, care for living things and family/community belonging.

activities.title: A familiar care greeting
activities.materials: Familiar caregiver; the usual safe care space
activities.purpose: Make an everyday care transition understandable and reassuring.
steps: Notice whether the infant is awake and available.
Use the child’s name and a familiar gentle phrase before needed care.
Pause for a cue, respond and continue care sensitively.
activities.adultRole: Stay responsive; the phrase supports connection rather than delaying care.
activities.observe: The cue, response and what seemed to support comfort.
activities.nextOpportunity: Use the same helpful phrase at another care moment.
activities.safety: Follow approved care and positioning procedures; never delay food, comfort or needed care for a lesson.
activities.inclusion: Use home languages, signs, visual cues, adapted movement/tools and sufficient processing time. Watching or another comfortable response is participation; do not force touch, speech, singing or performance.
activities.familyConnection: Share one actual strength or preference and ask what the family notices at home. Any suggested home connection is optional and needs no purchase.

activities.title: Comfortable awake floor movement
activities.materials: Firm clear floor mat; adult within reach
activities.purpose: Offer voluntary movement without a required posture.
steps: Choose a comfortable awake moment.
Offer a safe position and room for the infant’s own movement.
Respond to cues and reposition or stop as needed.
activities.adultRole: Observe closely rather than placing the infant in a position they cannot manage.
activities.nextOpportunity: Repeat a comfortable opportunity when available.
activities.safety: Tummy time is awake and directly supervised only. For sleep use the approved firm flat clear surface on the back, following current health procedures. No loose play materials in the sleep space.
activities.inclusion: Use home languages, signs, visual cues, adapted movement/tools and sufficient processing time. Watching or another comfortable response is participation; do not force touch, speech, singing or performance.

activities.safety: No pesticides, sharp pruning, unknown fungi/plants, animal waste or wildlife disturbance. Follow local outdoor and hygiene procedures.
activities.inclusion: Use home languages, signs, visual cues, adapted movement/tools and sufficient processing time. Watching or another comfortable response is participation; do not force touch, speech, singing or performance.
activities.familyConnection: Share one actual strength or preference and ask what the family notices at home. Any suggested home connection is optional and needs no purchase.
